text: CHAPTER 7
speaker: Narrator

text: The Journal That Remembers
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: Zik woke with the taste of black water still in his mouth.
speaker: Narrator

text: It was brackish and heavy. He sat upright on the narrow pallet, breathing through his nose while the taste clung to the back of his throat. The room was small, hot, and familiar. A cracked clay basin sat beside the wall. His boots were where he had left them. The thin curtain over the window stirred once and fell still.
speaker: Narrator

text: The dream had been short. Darkness with weight. Pressure against his chest. A voice calling him by a name he had never heard.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not Zik.
speaker: Narrator

text: The other name.
speaker: Narrator

text: He swung his feet to the floor and stood. Through the window the city lay under morning fog, its black spires jutting upward like jagged teeth. Ordinary sounds reached him—a cart on uneven stone, a woman shouting, a dog that barked once and went silent.
speaker: Narrator

text: They helped.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik turned to the bedside table. His father's journal lay there, bound in worn leather. He had placed it there the night before and left it untouched.
speaker: Narrator

text: He picked it up.
speaker: Narrator

text: The cover was cool against his palm. Almost damp. He opened it to the last marked page—an inventory of supply costs from a failed expedition years ago. Rope. Water. Lamp oil. Grain. Replacement tools. The dull accounting his father had always preferred to any heroic story.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik almost closed the book again.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then he saw the writing beneath the numbers.
speaker: Narrator

text: Dark ink shimmered faintly in the dim morning light. Not faded. Not cracked with age. Wet enough to catch the light.
speaker: Narrator

text: He closed the journal.
speaker: Narrator

text: Maybe he had missed it. The thought arrived quickly, almost desperately. Perhaps the writing had been there all along. Perhaps the light had been wrong. Perhaps he was exhausted.
speaker: Narrator

text: He waited, then opened it again.
speaker: Narrator

text: The writing remained.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zikir, if you are reading this, the seal is failing.
speaker: Bel-iddin
note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

text: Zik stopped breathing.
speaker: Narrator

text: The next lines were written in a hand he knew better than his own.
speaker: Narrator

text: The First City is not a tomb.
speaker: Bel-iddin
note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

text: It is a lid.
speaker: Bel-iddin
note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

text: His fingers tightened on the edge of the page.
speaker: Narrator

text: Do not trust the symbol on your skin.
speaker: Bel-iddin
note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

text: It was never meant for you.
speaker: Bel-iddin
note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

text: The last line sat alone.
speaker: Narrator

text: You were never supposed to find me.
speaker: Bel-iddin
note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

text: Zik let the journal fall onto the bed.
speaker: Narrator

text: It landed open.
speaker: Narrator

text: The wet lines shone against the page.
speaker: Narrator

text: He stood over it, waiting for the ink to soak into the fibers or smear or do anything ordinary. It remained on the surface, black and glossy, as though the words had been written seconds ago by a hand that had only just withdrawn.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik reached toward the page.
speaker: Narrator

text: Stopped.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then went to the basin instead.
speaker: Narrator

text: A little water remained in the bottom from the night before. He dipped one finger into it and touched the edge of the final line.
speaker: Narrator

text: The ink did not run.
speaker: Narrator

text: The water did.
speaker: Narrator

text: It gathered into a bead against the page and rolled away without darkening the parchment.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik wiped his finger on his tunic.
speaker: Narrator

text: Fine.
speaker: Zik

text: The journal offered no opinion.
speaker: Narrator

text: He took the bronze awl from his pack and pressed its tip lightly into the margin beside the writing. The point left a pale indentation. The paper behaved like old paper.
speaker: Narrator

text: Only the ink refused.
speaker: Narrator

text: He turned back one page.
speaker: Narrator

text: Supply figures. A note about a cracked axle. His father's complaint that a guide had watered the beer and lied badly about it.
speaker: Narrator

text: The next page held a rough map of a canal settlement abandoned before Zik was born.
speaker: Narrator

text: Nothing unusual.
speaker: Narrator
